Module io.github.brantunger.unruly.core
Package io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.language

Interface EvaluationContext

All Known Subinterfaces:
ActionContext
public sealed interface EvaluationContext permits ActionContext (not exhaustive)
What a condition is evaluated against.

Implemented by the engine, which passes it to a language. It's sealed, so a language can't implement it; a language's unit tests create one with io.github.brantunger.unruly.test.LanguageTestContexts, from the unruly-engine-test artifact. Because only the engine implements it, a later release can add methods to it without breaking languages.

    • isCancelled

      boolean isCancelled()
      Returns whether the run must stop, because its thread has been interrupted or it has passed its deadline.

      The engine checks this itself before each condition and each action, and again when each one returns, so a language that evaluates an expression and returns needn't. A language whose expressions can stop part-way polls it, or maps it to its own cancellation, so a long-running expression stops too. Returning any value is enough: the engine stops the run as soon as the expression returns, whatever it returned. Throwing an exception once the run is cancelled stops the run the same way; an Error, or an exception with one anywhere in its cause chain, such as one wrapping what a fact's Java code threw, is still that rule's failure. A language that can't stop inside an expression runs it to its end, and the run stops when it returns.

      Returns:
      true if the run must stop

    • deadline

      @Nullable Instant deadline()
      Returns when the run must stop, from the timeout its engine or its run call was given.
      Returns:
      The deadline, or null if the run has none. isCancelled() already accounts for it; a language can use it to give a call of its own a timeout.
